_comment: Security headers, secure-by-default. Feature 36, SECHDR-DEC-01/02.
The SecurityHeadersMiddleware existed in all four with byte-identical GOOD
defaults but was NEVER registered in any default middleware chain, so a
default Tina4 app shipped with NO clickjacking/MIME/CSP protection unless the
developer knew to opt in (SECHDR-OFF-BY-DEFAULT). And HSTS had no HTTPS guard:
with TINA4_HSTS set it would be emitted on plain HTTP too
(SECHDR-HSTS-NO-HTTPS-GUARD). There was ZERO test coverage (SECHDR-ZERO-TESTS).
PHP's class was SecurityHeaders, diverging from the other three's
SecurityHeadersMiddleware (SECHDR-CLASS-NAME-DIVERGE). See
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/features/036-security-headers.md and
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/OWNER-DECISIONS.md (Batch 1, SECHDR-DEC-01).
SECHDR-DEC-01 makes it secure-by-default, in all four:
1. REGISTER SecurityHeadersMiddleware in the DEFAULT middleware chain at
boot, UNCONDITIONALLY (no opt-in) -- a default app emits the headers.
2. HTTPS-guard HSTS: emit Strict-Transport-Security ONLY on an HTTPS request
(proxy-aware: x-forwarded-proto first hop, then the native TLS scheme),
NEVER on plain HTTP -- reusing each framework's existing secure-scheme
detector (Python request.is_secure_scheme(), PHP Request::isSecureScheme(),
Ruby Request.secure_scheme?(env), Node x-forwarded-proto + socket.encrypted).
3. CSP default-src 'self' by default (relax via TINA4_CSP).
4. PHP's class renamed SecurityHeaders -> SecurityHeadersMiddleware (parity).
5. The canonical header set + exact VALUES are identical across the four
(X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, CSP
default-src 'self', Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin,
X-XSS-Protection 0, Permissions-Policy camera=(), microphone=(),
geolocation=()). HTTP header names are case-insensitive; the tests compare
names case-insensitively and values byte-exactly.
MIGRATION (breaking, documented in the feature doc + commit body): registering
by default changes every app's response headers. CSP default-src 'self' blocks
inline <script>/<style> and third-party CDNs -- an app that needs them sets
TINA4_CSP (e.g. "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' cdn.example").
Every case runs through the REAL request pipeline of each framework with NO
MOCKS: Python drives tina4_python.core.server.handle with a real ASGI scope and
reads response._headers; PHP drives Router::dispatch with a real Request and
reads the Response headers; Ruby drives the real Tina4::RackApp#call (the object
Puma calls) with a real Rack env; Node boots a REAL @tina4/core server via
startServer and makes REAL HTTP requests, asserting the actual emitted headers.
The middleware is attached exactly the way boot attaches it (the same
registration call the framework makes), never a per-test hand-wire that a real
app would not do.
Mutation-proved (macOS, all four): unregistering the middleware turns the
canonical-set case RED (the default app then carries none of the headers);
dropping the HTTPS guard (emit HSTS on any scheme) turns the
hsts-absent-on-plain-http case RED. Restoring each returns to green.
Each invariant names a REAL suite file per framework and a list of case names;
the four suites carry the SAME case names in each language's own idiom, which
scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py normalises and matches.
feature: 36 - Security headers (secure-by-default register + HTTPS-guarded HSTS + CSP default-src 'self')

invariants.rule: SecurityHeadersMiddleware is registered in the DEFAULT middleware chain at boot, unconditionally (no opt-in). A default Tina4 app response therefore carries the canonical security header set with byte-identical VALUES across the four frameworks -- X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self', Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin, X-XSS-Protection: 0, Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=() -- with header names compared case-insensitively (HTTP is case-insensitive). CSP defaults to default-src 'self' (relax via TINA4_CSP).
invariants.why: The middleware shipped OFF in all four (never registered), so a default app had no clickjacking/MIME/CSP protection -- the exact SECHDR-OFF-BY-DEFAULT gap. Registering it at boot makes Tina4 secure-by-default. Mutation-proved: unregistering the middleware makes the default app carry none of these headers and this case goes RED.
cases: a default app response carries the canonical security header set
csp defaults to default src self

invariants.rule: Strict-Transport-Security is emitted ONLY on an HTTPS request (proxy-aware: x-forwarded-proto first hop, else the native TLS scheme) and is ABSENT on a plain-HTTP request, even when TINA4_HSTS is set. When present it is exactly max-age=<TINA4_HSTS>; includeSubDomains.
invariants.why: HSTS had no scheme guard in any framework, so with TINA4_HSTS set it would be emitted on plain HTTP too -- a false HTTPS-only contract, and a bad max-age would go out on every scheme. Guarding it at the scheme makes the HTTPS-only contract real. Mutation-proved: dropping the guard (emit on any scheme) makes the hsts-absent-on-plain-http case go RED.
cases: hsts is present on an https request
hsts is absent on a plain http request
